column1: # boru Language Specification: CALLBACKS and higher-order shapes
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# The shapes REAL boru programs use when a function travels as a value:
# a fn handed to a word and applied; a fn parked in a map, a list, a
# class field or a flex store and called back later; a fn RETURNED by a
# fn; a closure over a parameter applied after its maker returned; a
# callback driven by each / fold / filter / for-each; a fn-valued
# argument with a declared Function (or fnsig) type; apply in its
# several spellings; a curried chain; a callback that itself takes a
# callback.
# EVERY row's expected column is the value the INTERPRETER produces —
# measured, never guessed. Rows are then labelled with their
# BORU_FORCE_COMPILE=1 status, and the ones that FAIL TO COMPILE are recorded
# DELIBERATELY, as OPEN DEFECTS: the compiler scores ~96% on the old
# one-liner corpus and ~65% on real files precisely because a compile failure is
# WHOLE-PROGRAM and latches on the first unsupported construct, and the
# old corpus never combined constructs. A declining row is the point of
# this file; its description names the compile failure reason verbatim, so the
# reason text is the ledger of what is left to build.
# NOTE FOR THE RATCHET: test/go/langspec/compiled_coverage_test.go holds
# failureCeiling = 0. The declining rows below are new evidence, not
# regressions — the ceiling must be re-based (or this file moved under
# lang/spec/frontier/) when the corpus is next gated.
# §1  A fn VALUE passed and applied — the /v suffix, valof, /uv, chained
#     apply. The value is parked by /v and called by apply, by a bare
#     dispatch, or by a paren call.
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def f inc/v  f 5
column3: a def-bound fn value dispatches like a word (forward arg)

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def f inc/v  5 f
column3: …and from the stack (mirror equivalence)

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def f inc/v  def g f/v  (g 5)
column3: /v re-parks an already-parked fn value: the alias calls the same fn

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def f inc/v  5 f/v apply
column3: apply over a def-bound fn value

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  5 inc/v apply inc/v apply
column3: apply CHAINS — each result feeds the next application

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def dbl fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n mul 2]]  5 inc/v apply dbl/v apply
column3: a two-stage pipeline written as two applies

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  10 3 sub2/uv apply add 100
column3: the /uv (usurp) spelling reverses the signature order, and its result composes

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def g (valof inc)  (g 5)
column3: the (valof f) spelling parks the same value the /v suffix does

column1: def mk fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  5 (mk 1)/v apply
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "computed closure at a word's argument slot (its apply did not collapse — Stage 2)"

column1: def adder fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  10 (adder 3) apply
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "computed closure at a word's argument slot (its apply did not collapse — Stage 2)" — the closure is made and applied in one statement

column1: # §2  A fn STORED in a container — map, list, class field, flex store —
#     read back, then called. This is the plugin/handler-table idiom and
#     it is everywhere in real code.
def m {f: (fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]])}  def g m.f  (g 5)
column3: a map field read into a binding, then called

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def xs [inc/v]  (xs.0 5)
column3: a fn value in a LIST, called through an index

column1: def xs [(fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]]) (fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a mul 2]])]  (xs.1 5)
column3: a two-element dispatch table picks its second entry

column1: def xs [(fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]])]  5 (xs 0 get) apply
column3: get reads the fn out of the list and apply calls it

column1: def m {f: (fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]])}  5 (m 'f' get) apply
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "apply over a dynamic lead (overload unprovable)" — the same read spelled with get

column1: def m {f: (fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]])}  5 m.f/v apply
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "apply over a dynamic lead (overload unprovable)" — /v on a map field, applied

column1: def ops {inc: (fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]) dbl: (fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n mul 2]])}  (ops.inc (ops.dbl 5))
column3: two table entries composed at the call site

column1: def reg {handlers: [(fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]) (fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n mul 2]])]}  (reg.handlers.0 5)
column3: a handler list NESTED in a map, reached by a two-step path

column1: def reg {handlers: [(fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]) (fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n mul 2]])]}  each ([f:Function] => [(f 10)]) reg.handlers
column3: every handler in the table driven over one input

column1: def cbs {a: (fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]) b: (fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n mul 2]])}  each ([k:String] => [((cbs k get) 10)]) ['a' 'b']
column3: the table looked up BY KEY inside the callback

column1: def Handler class {cb: Function} def h (make Handler {cb: (fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]])}) (h.cb 5)
column3: a Function-typed CLASS FIELD holds the callback

column1: def Handler class {cb: Function} def h (make Handler {cb: (fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]])}) each h.cb [1 2 3]
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "higher-order `each` over a gradual-Any collection: ambiguous overload (List vs Map), no static commit and no poly re-match"

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def hold {f: inc/v}  each hold.f [1 2 3]
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: same gradual-Any each — the callback came out of a map field

column1: def mk fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  def fs [(mk 1) (mk 2)]  (fs.1 10)
column3: a LIST of computed closures, called by index

column1: def mk fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  def fs {a: (mk 1) b: (mk 2)}  (fs.b 10)
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "unannotated or opaque word dot" — the same closures in a MAP, called by name

column1: def reg (flex {}) end def h fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]] end reg set 'cb' h/v drop end ((reg.cb) 5)
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "function value reaches set (Stage 3)" — the mutable-registry idiom

column1: def reg (flex {}) end def h fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]] end reg set 'cb' h/v drop end typeof (reg.cb)
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "function value reaches set (Stage 3)" — even just reading the stored callback's type

column1: # §3  A fn RETURNED by a fn, then applied.
def mk fn [[][Function][(fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]])]]  5 (mk) apply
column3: a 0-arg factory's result applied straight away

column1: def mk fn [[][Function][(fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]])]]  def g (mk)  (g 5)
column3: …or bound first, then called

column1: def adder fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  def a3 (adder 3)  (a3 10)
column3: the classic adder factory: bind the result, call it later

column1: def mk fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  def f2 (mk 2)  def f3 (mk 3)  (f3 (f2 10))
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "def-bound computed fn `f3`: an argument is not an evaluation-fixed value (the read's statement window — Stage 1)"

column1: def sel fn [[b:Boolean][Function][if b [([n:Integer] => [n add 1])] [([n:Integer] => [n sub 1])]]]  ((sel true) 10)
column3: a fn chosen by a BRANCH and applied in the same statement

column1: def sel fn [[b:Boolean][Function][if b [([n:Integer] => [n add 1])] [([n:Integer] => [n sub 1])]]]  def f (sel false)  (f 10)
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "def-bound computed fn apply (closure shape unknown — Stage 1)" — the same branch result bound first

column1: def dispatch fn [[name:String][Function][if (name eq 'inc') [([n:Integer] => [n add 1])] [([n:Integer] => [n mul 2])]]]  ((dispatch 'inc') 5)
column3: a fn selected BY NAME — the string-keyed dispatcher idiom

column1: def hof fn [[f:Function][Function][f/v]]  def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def g (hof inc/v)  (g 4)
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "def-bound computed fn apply (closure shape unknown — Stage 1)" — identity over a fn value, bound and called

column1: def mk fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  def fs (each mk/v [1 2 3])  (fs.2 10)
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "fn-value application bounded by a paren (dynamic value precedes args)" — a LIST of closures built by each

column1: def mk fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  size (each mk/v [1 2 3])
column3: …building that list of closures is fine; only calling one back is not

column1: def mk fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  size (each [(mk 2)] [1 2 3])
column3: a closure made in an each BODY is collected as data, never fired

column1: # §4  CLOSURES — a lambda capturing a parameter or an enclosing binding,
#     applied after the capture site is gone.
def n 3  def f ([x:Integer] => [x mul n])  (f 4)
column3: a lambda captures an enclosing def and is called through its binding

column1: def n 3  def f ([x:Integer] => [x mul n])  5 f/v apply
column3: …and the same closure reached by apply

column1: def n 3  def f ([x:Integer] => [x mul n])  each f/v [1 2]
column3: …and driven as an each callback

column1: def mkadd fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  def a5 (mkadd 5)  each a5/v [1 2 3]
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "unmatched dispatch recovered at each" — a captured-param closure as an each callback

column1: def mkadd fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  def a5 (mkadd 5)  each [a5] [1 2 3]
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "code-body word each (Stage 2)" — the quotation spelling of the same call

column1: def counter fn [[start:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [start add n])]]  def c (counter 100)  fold [add] (each [c] [1 2 3]) 0
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "code-body word each (Stage 2)" — closure in an each body, result folded

column1: def mk fn [[k:Integer][Function][([n:Integer] => [n add k])]]  each ([k:Integer] => [((mk k) 100)]) [1 2 3]
column3: a closure MADE AND CALLED inside the callback compiles

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  def p ([b:Integer] => [sub2 10 b])  (p 3)
column3: partial application written by hand as a capturing lambda

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  each ([b:Integer] => [sub2 10 b]) [1 2 3]
column3: …driven over a list

column1: def sq fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n mul n]]  each ([x:Integer] => [(sq x) add 1]) [1 2 3]
column3: a named fn CALLED inside a lambda callback, its result post-processed

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def i 0  while [i lt 3] [def i (i inc/v apply)] end i
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "dynamic-scope def `i` of unpromoted computed value" — a callback applied in a LOOP body

column1: # §5  A callback DRIVEN by each / fold / filter / for-each.
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  [1 2 3] each inc/v
column3: an `fn`-form callback over a list (stack spelling)

column1: def sum2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a add b]]  0 fold sum2/v [1 2 3 4]
column3: a two-parameter fn value as a fold callback (accumulator, element)

column1: def sum2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a add b]]  fold sum2/v [1 2 3 4] 0
column3: …and the forward spelling of the same fold

column1: def kvsum fn [[acc:Integer kv:KeyVal][Integer][acc add kv.v]]  0 fold kvsum/v {a:1 b:2 c:3}
column3: a fold callback over a MAP receives (accumulator, KeyVal)

column1: def kvdbl fn [[kv:KeyVal][Integer][kv.v mul 2]]  each kvdbl/v {a:1 b:2}
column3: an each callback over a map receives the KeyVal and the shape is kept

column1: def ev fn [[p:Any][Boolean][(p.value mod 2) eq 0]]  filter ev/v [1 2 3 4 5 6]
column3: a named predicate as filter's Function form (list: {key value} pair)

column1: def kvf fn [[kv:KeyVal][Boolean][kv.v gt 2]]  filter kvf/v {a:1 b:5 c:3}
column3: …and over a map, where the predicate gets a KeyVal

column1: def pred fn [[p:Any][Boolean][p.value gt 2]]  fold [add] (filter pred/v [1 2 3 4]) 0
column3: filter's callback result feeding a fold — two higher-order words in one statement

column1: def acc (flex []) end def stp fn [[e:Integer][Any][acc push (e mul 2)]] end for-each stp/v [1 2 3] end acc
column3: a side-effecting callback accumulating into a flex list

column1: def acc (flex {}) end def stp fn [[kv:KeyVal][Any][acc set (kv.k) (kv.v mul 2)]] end for-each stp/v {a:1 b:2} end acc
column3: …and the map twin, keyed by the KeyVal's own key

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  each [inc/v apply] [1 2 3]
column3: apply INSIDE an each body, against the element on the stack

column1: def useit fn [[f:Function x:Integer][Integer][(f x)]]  def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  each [useit inc/v] [1 2 3]
column3: an each body that hands a fn value to a higher-order word

column1: def poly fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1] [s:String][String][s]]  each poly/v [1 2 3]
column3: a MULTI-OVERLOAD fn value as an each callback: the Integer signature is selected per element

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def dbl fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n mul 2]]  each ([f:Function] => [(f 5)]) [inc/v dbl/v]
column3: each over a LIST OF FUNCTIONS, applying every one to a fixed input

column1: def tag fn [[e:Integer][List][[e e]]]  each tag/v [1 2]
column3: a callback returning a LIST per element

column1: def sum fn [[xs:List][Integer][fold [add] xs 0]]  each sum/v [[1 2] [3 4]]
column3: a callback that folds its own argument — nested higher-order words

column1: each ([r:List] => [each ([x:Integer] => [x add 1]) r]) [[1 2] [3]]
column3: an each callback whose body is itself an each with a lambda

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  scan [add] (each inc/v [1 2 3])
column3: a mapped list fed to scan

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  fold [add] (each inc/v (each inc/v [1 2 3])) 0
column3: two callback passes piped into a fold in one statement

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def s (each inc/v [1 2 3])  fold [mul] s 1
column3: …and with the intermediate list bound between the two passes

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  0 fold ([acc:Integer e:Integer] => [acc add (e inc/v apply)]) [1 2 3]
column3: apply inside a fold LAMBDA

column1: # §6  A fn-valued ARGUMENT with a declared type — `Function`, or a named
#     fnsig — and what a body may do with it.
def useit fn [[f:Function x:Integer][Integer][(f x)]]  def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  useit inc/v 5
column3: the plain Function parameter, applied in the body

column1: def useit fn [[f:Function x:Integer][Integer][(f x)]]  def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  5 inc/v useit
column3: …the full-stack spelling of the same call

column1: def twice fn [[f:Function x:Integer][Integer][(f (f x))]]  twice ([n:Integer] => [n mul 3]) 2
column3: the callback applied TWICE in one body, with a lambda argument

column1: def cb fn [[f:Function][Integer][(f 10)]]  cb ([n:Integer] => [n add 5])
column3: an anonymous lambda passed straight into a Function parameter

column1: def twice fn [[f:Function x:Integer][Integer][(f (f x))]]  def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  twice inc/v 5
column3: …and the named-fn argument of the same doubly-applying word

column1: def apply2 fn [[f:Function g:Function x:Integer][Integer][(f (g x))]]  def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  def dbl fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n mul 2]]  apply2 inc/v dbl/v 5
column3: TWO Function parameters composed inside the body

column1: def IntToInt fnsig Integer Integer  def useit fn [[g:IntToInt x:Integer][Integer][(g x)]]  def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  useit inc/v 7

column1: def IntToInt fnsig Integer Integer  def useit fn [[g:IntToInt][Function][g/v]]  def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  typeof (useit inc/v)

column1: def apply1 fn [[f:Function x:Integer][Integer][x f/v apply]]  def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  apply1 inc/v 5
column3: apply at the TAIL of a fn body over the body's own Function parameter

column1: def apply-twice fn [[f:Function x:Integer][Integer][x f/v apply f/v apply]]  def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  apply-twice inc/v 5

column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "function-valued operand at each (Stage 3)" — the generic map helper, THE commonest real-code callback shape

column1: def each2 fn [[f:Function xs:List][List][each f/v xs]]  each2 ([n:Integer] => [n mul 2]) [1 2 3]
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "function-valued operand at each (Stage 3)" — same helper, lambda argument

column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: "function-valued operand at fold (Stage 3)" — the generic reduce helper

column1: def tap fn [[f:Function xs:List][List][each ([e:Integer] => [(f e)]) xs]]  def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  tap inc/v [1 2 3]

column1: # §8  Module-exported callbacks — the export map is a callback table.

column1: # §9  CURRIED CHAINS and the boru:fn-util combinators.
def mk3 fn [[a:Integer][Function][([b:Integer] => [([c:Integer] => [(a add b) add c])])]]  def f1 (mk3 1)  def f2 (f1 2)  (f2 3)

column1: # §10  A FN VALUE APPLIED BY A HIGHER-ORDER WORD OPENS ITS OWN FRAME, whose
#      `args` is the value's own call args (NUR166, closed 2026-09-25: the
#      compiled callback body read the enclosing frame's list — none at the
#      top level — so `do [args]` inside it raised `args: not inside a
#      function` per element). A quotation body runs in the CALLER's frame
#      and reads the caller's args, on both lanes.
def g fn [[n:Integer] [Any] [do [args]]] end each g/v [1 2]
column3: a named fn value's body reads its own call args, even through a `do` body

column1: def g fn [[n:Integer] [Any] [do [args] size]] end each g/v [1 2]
column3: …one arg per call

column1: def g ([n:Integer] => [do [args]]) end each g/v [1 2]
column3: a lambda value too

column1: def h fn [[a:Integer] [Any] [do [args]]] end def w fn [[x:Integer] [Any] [each h/v [x 5]]] end w 7
column3: …and inside a fn: the value's frame, not the enclosing fn's

column1: def w fn [[x:Integer] [Any] [each [do [args]] [x 5]]] end w 7
column3: a QUOTATION body runs in the caller's frame: the enclosing fn's args

column1: # §11  A NAMED VALUE'S NO-MATCH ON THE SEAM IS THE WORD'S RAISE (NUR211, closed
#      2026-09-25): a named fn value driving fold whose signature stops
#      matching past the first step raises uncalled_function, as the word
#      does; an anonymous lambda's no-match leaves the value as data (NUR155).
def h fn [[a:Integer b:Integer] [List] [[a b]]] end 0 fold h/v [1 2]
